# P32.4 — Unify bitemporal occurrence selection across all readers

PR **#159** (https://github.com/SteveVitali/Eleutheria/pull/159) · base `devin/p32-3-roles-counts-and-organization-identity` · branch
`devin/p32-4-shared-temporal-read-contract` · run
`implement-spec spec=docs/tickets/164_P32.4__shared-temporal-read-contract.md live_verification=false`
(full rigor) · BUILD_INDEX row 164 · stream **S1** — Round 10.

## Requirement ids

**SIG-TRUST-005** (§55); cites **BL-058** / S1 evidence-integrity research. **ADR-123**.

## Summary

One shared `temporal-read/1` contract — **eligible-occurrence selection** — now governs every
reader that previously defined "latest evidence" for itself. The contract is owned in
`db/src/db/occurrences.py` (pure conformance model + SQL fragment builders) and mirrored exactly
by the sqitch `eligible_occurrence(claim_id, belief)` function: `role = 'establishes'`,
`bound_at <= belief`, ordered `retrieved_at DESC NULLS LAST` with `capture_id ASC` as the
deterministic tie-break — `capture_id`/`claim_id` are *never* clocks. Claim visibility is bounded
separately on the valid-world axis (`claim.sys_period @> belief`), and undated claims fall back
to the selected occurrence's `retrieved_at` under the labelled basis
`capture_retrieved_at_latest`. Historical outputs stay frozen: nothing written later can redact a
past-belief read.

- **`db/`** — `occurrences.py`: `select_occurrence`/`select_observation` (with basis labels),
  `lineage_candidates` (per-source-lineage latest), `occurrence_lateral`/`belief_expression` SQL
  builders (`BELIEF_PARAM`/`BELIEF_NOW`), and the bounded `spine_watermark` read. Sqitch
  **`shared_temporal_contract`** (deploy/revert/verify): the `eligible_occurrence` SQL twin;
  **`camera_site_execution`** — append-only per-*execution* completion references; and the
  trigger-maintained **`spine_watermark`** table closing **D-P31.1-1**.
- **`reconcile/`** — `Claim.observed_instant` (exact ordering instant beside date-only
  `observed_at`) + occurrence refs (`occurrence_capture_id`/`occurrence_retrieved_at`/
  `occurrence_bound_at`); `digest_token` includes the instant so a same-day re-sighting is a new
  input; `read_claim_groups` selects through the shared lateral with an explicit belief bound.
- **`resolution/`** — `read_camera_records` selects the per-predicate latest eligible occurrence;
  coordinate pairs resolve only from **one common occurrence** (lat and lon are never mixed
  across captures, `coordinate_capture_id` preserved); `camera_site_run` stays digest-keyed while
  each execution appends its own `camera_site_execution`; `read_resolved_site_runs` follows the
  **latest completed execution**.
- **`api/`** — `_public_claim_groups`/`claims_for`/`stored_claim` select through the shared
  lateral (`BELIEF_PARAM` for frozen reads, `BELIEF_NOW` for current); `_spine_watermark` is now
  an O(27 facets) table read (legacy six-count fallback for pre-change dumps) — the ~10 s
  per-request full-spine scan is gone.
- **`exports/`** — `shaping_claims` carries occurrence refs + a belief-bounded claim-source CTE
  on the same instant as its `sys_period` filter (`{EFFECTIVE}` markers expanded by
  `expand_query`); envelope candidates are per-source-lineage latest (independent sources stay
  concurrent; superseded members remain labelled history); the spine export freshness read uses
  the bounded watermark inside the existing `REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY` snapshot.

## Camera-site execution semantics (ticket ACs)

- Every execution appends its own `camera_site_execution` completion row — **A→B→A** re-executes
  A's digest, finds the existing `camera_site_run` (`run_record_inserted=False`), and still
  appends a new completion, so `read_resolved_site_runs` returns run A and no reader is left on B.
- Retrying the same `execution_id` is **+0** (idempotent).
- Existing `camera_site_run` rows are backfilled with one honest execution reference each.

## Watermark (D-P31.1-1 → DONE)

`spine_watermark` is one row per watched facet (~27) maintained by statement-level
SECURITY DEFINER triggers on INSERT, the sole permitted `sys_period`-close UPDATE (adds
`closed_count` only — transition tables are split per event; PG forbids multi-event transition
tables), and TRUNCATE. It is bumped in the same transaction as the write — snapshot-consistent,
never stale, over-invalidation only (a deliberately bounded "at least the affected state"
contract). Verified on real PG18 for all three required classes: new claims, corrections, and
completed materializations.

**Measured at the hosted defect's exact scale** (`p31-scale-local` — 2.3M claims + 2.3M
bindings, full production sqitch plan, local Docker PG18; `docs/build/reports/p32.4-watermark/RESULTS.md`,
reproduce `docs/build/tools/measure_watermark_p31.py`): named budget warm p99 < 10 ms /
8-way p99 < 50 ms — measured **warm p99 1.81 ms, 8-way p99 37.7 ms** (200 calls, 138 ms
wall) vs the legacy six-count scan's 8-way median 5.0 s / max 12.2 s at the same scale
(~316×); plan = 4 shared-hit blocks, no claim-spine scan. Local deterministic evidence
only — composed/hosted serving verification stays reserved to the scheduled e2e row.

## Deferrals

**Closed D-P31.1-1** (annotation watermark engineering defect; hosted verify reserved). Opened
none.

## Deviations

Recorded in `docs/build/runs/P32.4.md`: resolver Phase 1.4 keeps its `(source, valid window)`
supersession key using the shared `ordering_instant` axis; the camera reader stays
current-knowledge (`BELIEF_NOW`) as it feeds live materialization; the watermark intentionally
over-invalidates globally rather than tracking per-claim staleness.

## Guardrails

No UPDATE/DELETE on the claim spine; append-only throughout (the only UPDATE path is the
trigger-maintained watermark, internal to the design). No gate ticked, no source flipped, no
merge/tag/push to `main`.
